Limitation: comparable PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2 or incremental AUROC) are not provided for any candidate, and several reported full-model AUROCs (e.g., 0.79 for PGS005219; 0.77 for PGS003857/PGS003858) are not directly interpretable as standalone PRS performance; additionally, PGS005219 is BMI-adjusted, which may affect comparability depending on the intended sleep-apnea definition.

Direct-match candidates are present for sleep apnea, including multiple generic “Sleep apnea” models (PGS003204–PGS003218) and clinically dominant subtype “Obstructive sleep apnea” models (PGS003479, PGS003857/PGS003858, PGS005219/PGS005220). Per the provided domain knowledge, obstructive sleep apnea is the dominant clinical form of sleep apnea and is therefore an acceptable direct match when better supported. Among OSA candidates, PGS005219 shows the strongest visible PRS-relevant evidence: highest reported effect size (OR=1.98, 95% CI 1.74–2.24) and the highest reported AUROC (0.79, though it is full-model and includes BMI), with a multi-score aggregation method (“weighted PRSsummation PRS-CSs”) and multi-cohort training (FinnGen, MGBB, MVP). Main limitation: across the pool, reported AUROCs are full-model (covariate-including) rather than PRS-only, and key details are missing/ambiguous for some strong-looking alternatives (e.g., PGS003857/PGS003858 have AUROC=0.77 but it is also full-model with BMI adjustment and their PRS effect sizes are much smaller), so the evidence supports a preference but not a high-certainty selection.

All 20 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported and/or trait_efo align to bladder cancer; phenotyping is generally bladder cancer/"cancer of bladder", with one urothelial carcinoma). No model reports PRS-only AUROC/R2, so full-model AUROC is not directly comparable as a PRS metric; selection therefore relies mainly on endpoint fidelity plus effect-size evidence and basic covariate design. Among the best-supported options, PGS000611 (GWAS Hits, 13 variants; UKB-trained; EUR eval) reports a relatively strong per-SD effect (OR=1.284, 95% CI 1.211–1.361) and a notably higher extreme-tail separation (OR top 1% vs rest = 2.66, 95% CI 1.79–3.93) with a coherent bladder cancer endpoint and basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs). Competing near-clones (PGS000610/PGS000612, MGI-based) show similar per-SD OR but weaker top-1% evidence; PGS000613 has slightly higher per-SD OR and top-1% OR but differences are small and both are UKB-based, making them hard to distinguish from the visible metadata alone. Confidence is therefore moderate and the outcome is sub-optimal because PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2 or incremental metrics) are missing across candidates, limiting a clearly high-quality recommendation.

All 20 candidates are direct matches to urinary bladder cancer (trait_reported bladder cancer; trait_efo urinary bladder carcinoma/cancer; phenotyping_reported bladder cancer/incident bladder cancer/cancer of bladder/urothelial carcinoma). However, across the pool there are no clearly reported PRS-only (covariate-free) AUROC/R² metrics, so ranking relies on endpoint fidelity plus available effect-size/full-model metrics and structural signals, which limits certainty.

PGS000613 is preferred because it has strong endpoint alignment ('Cancer of bladder'), is part of the coherent Cancer PRSweb bladder-cancer cluster with comparable basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), and shows among the strongest visible discriminative evidence within that cluster: full-model AUROC 0.571 with a relatively strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.301, 95% CI 1.227–1.379) and strong tail separation (OR top 1% vs rest 2.91, 95% CI 1.99–4.24). It also benefits from a larger development/training sample (n=12,992; UKB) than several near-identical siblings (e.g., n=7,469; MGI) while keeping the same endpoint family.

Main limitation: the best-looking full-model AUROCs in the set (e.g., PGS000071/PGS000782 ~0.80) are not PRS-only and are likely boosted by non-genetic covariates (notably smoking variables and BMI), making them non-comparable as evidence of PRS strength; meanwhile, several other candidates (e.g., PGS000611) have similar AUROC/OR evidence, so the superiority of PGS000613 is not decisive from the visible metadata alone.

All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (trait_efo=angina pectoris) with endpoint descriptions ranging from generic angina to ICD10 I20 and PheCode 411.3. Among models with clearly PRS-comparable metrics, PGS001262 reports the strongest PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC(no covariates)=0.58683; PGS R2(no covariates)=0.01304) and the largest incremental AUROC (0.0098) in European validation, with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, array type), and its PRS-only R2 remains well below the provided heritability ceiling sanity-check (h2_obs=0.0092; h2_liability=0.1337), avoiding obvious metric inconsistency. All 15 candidates are direct matches to glaucoma or its dominant clinical subtype POAG. Among disease-focused POAG models, PGS001792 (PRS-CS-auto) has a large evaluation sample (n=347,396), a PRS-comparable metric reported (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.03209), and a strong full-model AUROC (0.777) with only basic demographic/PC covariates (no family history/biomarker packaging). Limitation: evidence is still incomplete/incomparable across models (many lack PRS-only AUROC/R2; several report only full-model metrics), and PGS001792’s GWAS ancestry distribution metadata is internally unclear (‘OTH 90%’), so the preference is supported but not definitive.

All 15 candidates are direct matches for glaucoma or its major subtype POAG. All 15 candidates are direct matches to the target (glaucoma broadly or primary open-angle glaucoma). The main limitation is that many models report only full-model AUROC or partial correlations and covariate sets differ; even for PGS001792 the reported AUROC is full-model (0.777) and is not directly comparable as PRS-only discrimination, so the selection remains somewhat uncertain among several strong POAG/glaucoma candidates (e.g., PGS004944, PGS000137) with different endpoint/covariate/metric reporting.

All 15 candidates are direct matches to glaucoma or its major subtype POAG, with generally acceptable endpoint alignment. All 15 candidates are direct matches to the target trait glaucoma (or the dominant clinical subtype primary open-angle glaucoma), so a direct match exists. Direct-match candidates for the target trait (lymphoid/lymphocytic leukemia) are present (e.g., PGS000077, PGS000645, PGS000788, PGS002305). Direct-match candidates for the target concept (lymphoid/lymphocytic leukemia) are present (e.g., PGS000077, PGS000645, PGS000788, PGS002305). All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target concept (lymphoid/lymphocytic leukemia, including chronic lymphocytic leukemia subtypes).
